## Question

<div class="chapter-question">When a research agent searches, extracts, analyzes and writes, how can a human verify where each claim came from?</div>

## Why this week belongs here

The first research-agent session introduces planning, tool use, state and long-horizon failure. It connects the division of research labor to claim-level provenance.

## Provisional core readings

- Barrie et al. (2026), §10.5. [Download chapter PDF](../downloads/readings/ai-and-research-methods-barrie-et-al-2026.pdf). [@BarrieEtAl2026AIResearchMethods]
- Lu et al. (2026), “Towards End-to-End Automation of AI Research.” [@LuEtAl2026AIScientist]
- *Nature Machine Intelligence* (2026), “Multi-Agent AI Systems Need Transparency.” [@NatureMITransparency2026]
- Further reporting context: Feuerriegel et al. (2026). [@FeuerriegelEtAl2026]

## Planned chapter and class arc

Introduce agent trajectories and long-horizon tasks; examine current systems and benchmarks, including CRUX and recent Meta work; localize errors across retrieval, extraction, code and synthesis; finish with a human-verifiable claim/source table.

[See the provisional Week 11 Python plan](../python/session11.qmd).
